TERMS/create: terms in key-terms.md with no existing notes produce concept notes in wiki/concepts/ with aliases parsed, verbatim source block stored, History stamped, domain: concepts; lexicon regenerated. Content above the '---' separator (including the fenced example) must NOT be parsed as terms.

TERMS/change-detection: one term's text edited, others untouched. ONLY the edited note changes — verify by hashing every concept note before and after; untouched notes must be byte-identical. Edited note bumps updated and gains a History line containing the prior text.

TERMS/archive: a key-terms.md-sourced term removed from that file sets status: archived, appends a History line, moves to the lexicon's archived section. File still on disk; inbound wikilinks still resolve; git records a modification, not a deletion.

TERMS/precedence: the same term in key-terms.md and as a [define] line resolves to key-terms.md; the rejected text is recorded in History and flagged in the report when it disagrees substantively. Even when the winning source block is unchanged, the note IS touched to record the loser.
PROFILE: an item needing an undeclared type is filed under the closest declared type and the new type is PROPOSED in the report, never self-authorized.
evals.status: manually-verified 2026-08-12 (undeclared-type half only; the 'fits no declared domain -> default domain' half is still UNTESTED)

evals.prompt: Compile the knowledge base twice in a row.
evals.expected_output: REGRESSION (bug found 2026-08-12): a term created from a [define] marker has source: inbox. The first compile clears that marker from inbox.md. The SECOND compile must leave the note completely alone — status stays active, file unchanged. Archiving on absence applies only to notes with source: key-terms.md. Before the fix, every [define]-sourced term self-destructed on its second compile.
